title: Epic Games Puts $65,000 Behind AI-Built Games in Four-Day MegaJam
excerpt: The 2026 Epic AI MegaJam runs November 12-15 with teams of up to five and unlimited AI agents — and, after a same-day correction, AI use that is encouraged but not mandatory.
body:
• Epic Games' 2026 AI MegaJam runs November 12-15, 2026: teams of up to five people, plus unlimited AI agents, build a playable game in Unreal Engine or UEFN in four days.
  • The official jam page lists $65,000 in cash prizes — top main-category prize $7,500 — plus Development Continuation Grants of up to $50,000 per team; the $50,000 in early headlines is the grant ceiling and the jam's own tagline, not the cash pool.
  • AI is encouraged but not required: Epic corrected its FAQ the same day, saying the original mandatory-AI wording was a mistake.
  • Entry is open online from anywhere to developers aged 18 or over with an active Epic Games account — register on the official itch.io jam page, watch the theme reveal on November 11, and submit by November 15 at 5:59 PM PST.

Epic Games is offering serious money to developers who build a game with AI help in four days. The 2026 Epic AI MegaJam, announced on October 22, runs from November 12 to November 15 and asks teams to produce a playable game in Unreal Engine or Unreal Editor for Fortnite (UEFN), using as many AI agents as they want alongside up to five human teammates. The official AI MegaJam page on itch.io lists $65,000 in cash prizes, with Development Continuation Grants of up to $50,000 per team for standout entries.

How the MegaJam Works

The theme is revealed at a kickoff livestream on November 11 at 11 AM PST, and building opens at midnight EST on November 12. Nothing may be built before that date, though installing the engine and getting coding agents and MCP (Model Context Protocol) working in advance is encouraged. Entrants pick one track — Unreal Engine or UEFN, not both — and may use any AI tools they like, from coding agents to asset generation, audio and writing tools. Unreal Engine teams submit a packaged build under 1 GB through itch.io; UEFN teams submit a private version code. Every entry needs a 30-60 second gameplay video and team details, and the deadline is November 15 at 5:59 PM PST. Judges score entries from 1 to 5 on ambition and innovation, theme, fun factor, gameplay, visuals, level design and audio, with winners announced by January 29, 2027.

The Prize Money, Reconciled

Early coverage put three different figures on the same event — $50,000, $65,000 and, in NDTV's headline, Rs 47 lakh. The official jam page settles it. The cash pool is $65,000: the three main categories — Best Overall in Unreal Engine, Best Overall in UEFN, and Best Student Project — each pay $7,500 for first place, $5,000 for second and $2,500 for third, and modifier categories add $5,000 for Best Team and $2,500 each for best solo project, best visuals, best dev log, best narrative UEFN game and best mobile game in each track. Separately, continuation grants of $50,000, $25,000 and $10,000 per track sit outside the cash pool — the $50,000 figure in the jam's "Vibe your way to $50k" tagline and in several headlines.

AI Encouraged, Not Required

The announcement drew immediate criticism from developers, and the original FAQ — which said AI use was mandatory — was corrected the same day. Epic's Unreal Engine account acknowledged the error publicly:

"Our FAQ originally said you had to use AI for the MegaJam. That's our mistake. You can use as little or as much AI as you want. We're updating the FAQ and rules to make that clear."

— Unreal Engine (@UnrealEngine), October 22, 2026

The pushback went beyond the FAQ. Developers noted that game jams have produced weekend prototypes for decades — Ludum Dare has run since 2002 — and questioned marketing that presented AI as what makes a four-day build possible. The jam also lands inside a broader shift at Epic: CEO Tim Sweeney has described an AI-first pivot at the company, and Epic recently described its redesigned launcher as vibe-coded.

What It Means for Indian Developers

The jam is fully online, so developers in India — and Indian developers abroad — compete on the same terms as everyone else: aged 18 or over, an active Epic Games account, and one engine track. An in-person option runs at Digital Jungle in San Francisco on November 14-15, where teams from Anthropic, Google, OpenAI, Meshy and SpaceXSI are expected to build alongside entrants; San Francisco registration opens November 1 on Eventbrite and space is limited. Entrants keep ownership of the games they make. For independent developers weighing it, the realistic prize is twofold: a share of the $65,000 pool in November, and a shot at a continuation grant of up to $50,000 to turn a four-day prototype into a finished game.
